title: Cascade stall analysis and customer communication playbook for Hosted API 5xx/timeouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: During a multi-customer escalation window we observed recurring 5xx errors and request timeouts on the Hosted API. This ticket captures the investigation, the technical fixes applied across the serving runtime and edge proxies, SDK guidance to reduce amplification, and a reusable customer communication/playbook for future escalations.
impact_summary: Between 2025-02-11 03:40 UTC and 2025-02-12 07:10 UTC multiple customers experienced elevated 5xx rates and request timeouts. Root symptoms: long tail request latency, connection stalls on a subset of serving nodes, and cascading retry amplification causing queue saturation. Estimated affected requests: ~1.2M tokens/24h across 6 tenants; two high-touch customers reported degraded production SLAs.
timeline: 2025-02-11 03:45 - first alert from SRE on elevated 5xx. 04:10 - scoped to a cluster (cluster-eu-2). 04:35 - replicated locally; reproduced long GC-like stall in runtime with blocked send path. 05:00 - temporary mitigation: route traffic away from cluster and enable model-fallback. 06:20 - hotfix PR deployed to edge proxies to enforce client retry headers and early rejection for overloaded connection pools. 08:00 - runtime patch merged to fix allocator path. 12:00 - full rollout to all nodes behind feature-flagged gate. 2025-02-12 07:10 - incident declared resolved. Postmortem published 2025-02-18.
root_cause: A rare interaction between our custom slab allocator in the inference runtime and concurrent KV cache eviction logic caused sporadic memory fragmentation leading to short (50-300ms) blocking stalls in the token emission path. When stalls occurred, client SDKs and customers retried aggressively (some with no jitter), producing retry amplification that saturated connection queues in fronting proxies and produced 502/503/504s. The combination of allocator stalls + retry amplification produced a cascade rather than a single failing node.
corrective_actions: Patched slab allocator to avoid compaction on fast-path (runtime-PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1128)
Added a short async flush for KV cache eviction to break synchronous eviction-path stalls (runtime-PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1130)
Implemented server-side idempotency token acceptance header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) and dedupe logic at the front proxy to collapse duplicate retries
Introduce a server-enforced Retry-After header and per-origin token bucket on retries at the API gateway
SDK update: default optimistic jitter and client-side backoff policy with exponential backoff cap (sdk-js v2.6.1, sdk-py 1.9.0)
Circuit-breaker and dynamic shedding feature added to edge proxies for sustained connection queue depth (configurable via console)
Customer communication templates and SLA runbook created and stored in Drive (link below)
mitigations_deployed: Edge proxy hotfix to return 429+Retry-After for overloaded connection pools (deployed 2025-02-11 05:20 UTC)
Traffic steering away from affected cluster while patch rolled out (feature-flag gate)
Runtime patch rolled under canary and then full rollout (completed 2025-02-11 12:00 UTC)
SDK release notes and recommended retry knobs published to docs and emailed to top customers
rollout_notes: Runtime changes gated behind feature flag 'allocator-safety-2025-02'; Canary on 10% of nodes for 30 minutes, monitor fec, token emission latency P99, connection queue depth. Edge proxy changes were low-risk and pushed to all regions after 15 minutes of verification on canary.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-17655: Add automatic idempotency token generation in SDKs and guidance for server-side dedupe
ENG-17660: Increase observability for allocator metrics (per-slot fragmentation gauge)
PM-812: Update SLA language for retry amplification and mitigation timelines
DES-412: UI in Console to surface per-route retry policy and current shedding thresholds
customer_communication: We prepared a communication bundle for affected customers: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, technical summary within 24 hours, and a root cause + corrective actions notice on resolution. Templates: https://drive.redwood.com/hosted-incidents/templates/customer-update-oscillations.md
lessons_learned: 1) Aggressive client retries without jitter amplify ephemeral runtime stalls into system-wide outages. 2) Server-side dedupe and explicit Retry-After are effective at breaking amplification cycles. 3) Observability must include allocator fragmentation metrics and connection queue depth as first-class indicators. 4) Playbooks and customer comms prepared ahead of time reduce noise during escalations.
runbook_updates: Added a new triage checklist: check connection-queue depth, allocator fragmentation, KV eviction latency, and top origin retry headers
Added explicit steps to steer traffic by region/cluster and enable model-fallback automatically
Documented communication cadence and contact matrix for high-touch customers
